expected_evidence: Geological: platinum/iridium anomalies and elevated platinum-group-element concentrations in YD boundary layer (~12,800 cal BP) sediments across North America
Geological: magnetic and glassy microspherules, nanodiamonds (hexagonal lonsdaleite), and melt-glass in the YD boundary layer
Geological: continent-wide 'black mat' organic-rich layer marking abrupt ecological transition at YD onset
Geological: soot/charcoal spikes indicating widespread biomass burning synchronous with onset

Astronomical: absence of a confirmed impact crater of appropriate age (expected if mechanism is an airburst rather than surface impact) or, alternatively, candidate crater structures (e.g., under Greenland ice) datable to ~12,900 cal BP
Astronomical: cosmic-ray-exposure or extraterrestrial isotope signatures (He-3, Ir) in ice cores from Greenland/Antarctica
Material/archaeological: disruption or thinning of Clovis-culture artifact layers directly above the boundary layer, evidence of contemporaneous megafaunal extinction horizon
Genetic: population bottleneck signatures in North American megafauna and Paleoindian human genomes dated to ~12,900 cal BP
Geological (meltwater linkage): glacial lake outburst/drainage evidence (e.g., Lake Agassiz routing changes) synchronous with both the proposed airburst and the onset of AMOC-disruption cooling

model_prior: this hypothesis corresponds to the real, actively debated 'Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis' (Firestone et al. 2007 and successors), for which proponents have published purported nanodiamond/spherule/platinum evidence at dozens of sites, but numerous independent labs have failed to replicate these findings and no confirmed impact crater has been identified as of my training knowledge — recalled from training, not from provided evidence text, so treat as unverified
response.rationale: Using the 'younger-dryas' period row (interval -10950 ≈ 12,950 BP aligns with YD onset, ~12,900 cal BP) rather than the unspecified label. The mechanism (cosmic-airburst causing/triggering a meltwater pulse which then drove YD-onset cooling) implies evidence should cluster in geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.70) categories, which have the highest detectability scores for this period — sediment/ice-core/boundary-layer stratigraphy from ~12,900 years ago is well within the range that can and does survive (e.g., varved lake sediments, ice cores, loess sections), so absence of such evidence would be informative, not merely a detectability artifact. Material/archaeological (0.35) and genetic (0.30) evidence are less likely to survive/be diagnostic at this age, and textual/linguistic/oral_tradition/iconographic are essentially null (pre-writing, pre-recorded oral tradition, near-zero for this period), so their absence is fully expected and uninformative. Blending across the evidence kinds most relevant to this specific claim (geological, astronomical, with lower weight to material/genetic), a composite detectability of ~0.55 seems appropriate — high enough that real evidence (or its absence) is meaningful, but not so high as to ignore the intrinsic difficulty of confirming causal mechanism (airburst vs. purely internal ice-sheet dynamics) 13,000 years after the fact. Model-prior (unverified, from training, not the provided evidence text): this scenario matches the real-world 'Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis,' for which claimed platinum/nanodiamond/spherule evidence exists but has had inconsistent replication success and remains a minority position in Quaternary science; no confirmed impact crater has been identified. Given that geological/astronomical detectability is moderate-to-high for this period, a genuine cosmic-airburst-to-meltwater-pulse causal chain, if true, plausibly could have left recoverable traces — so the persistent lack of a firm scientific consensus is more consistent with contested/weak evidence than with pure undetectability.
